findings.reason: The protected SQL solution reports monthly active drivers and accepted rides for all 12 months of 2020. It uses a WITH RECURSIVE Months CTE (1 to 12) left joined to Rides and AcceptedRides, alongside a correlated scalar subquery counting Drivers with join_date prior to month + 1. The query runs in O(d + r + a) time and O(a) space; no candidate is required.
Recursive CTE generates full 12-month spine, correlated scalar subquery accurately counts cumulative active drivers, and LEFT JOIN onto AcceptedRides correctly counts monthly accepted rides.
Scanning d drivers, r rides, and a accepted rides over 12 months takes O(d + r + a) time and O(a) space for join aggregation buffers. Complexity evidence is bounded-domain certified and hash-bound.
Accepts Drivers, Rides, and AcceptedRides tables, returning 12 rows with columns month, active_drivers, and accepted_rides sorted by month ASC.

The approach accurately details 12-month CTE spine generation, accepted ride counting by request month, cumulative active driver cutoff logic, and O(d + r + a) time / O(a) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover ride-only grouping omission risks, rejected request inclusion errors, string format comparison hazards, pre-2020 driver inclusions, month-end boundary join dates, and non-2020 ride exclusions.
